slides.slide_title: Introduce y as /aɪ/ — second y sound
slides.teacher_cue: y has a second sound. When y appears at the END of a one-syllable word, it makes the long /aɪ/ sound — the same sound as the letter i says its name. my, by, try, fly, sky. This is y's second sound. y at the START of a word = /j/ consonant (yes, yell — taught at Lesson 20). y at the END of a one-syllable word = /aɪ/ (my, fly — today's lesson).
slides.expected_response: Students produce /aɪ/ cleanly and understand that y at the end of a one-syllable word makes /aɪ/.
slides.correction_move: Review: y as consonant /j/ (yes, yell). Contrast with y as /aɪ/ (my, fly). Establish the rule: position and syllable count determine the sound.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students producing /j/ for y at the end of words. Redirect with the position rule.
